# gdu - go DiskUsage()

Pretty fast disk usage analyzer written in Go.

Gdu is intended primarily for SSD disks where it can fully utilize parallel processing.
However HDDs work as well, but the performance gain is not so huge.

## Installation

Head for the [releases page](https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases) and download the binary for your system.

Using curl:

    curl -L https://github.com/dundee/gdu/releases/latest/download/gdu_linux_amd64.tgz | tar xz
    chmod +x gdu_linux_amd64
    mv gdu_linux_amd64 /usr/bin/gdu

Or you can use Gdu directly via Docker:

    docker run --rm --init --interactive --tty --privileged --volume /:/mnt/root ghcr.io/dundee/gdu /mnt/root

See [INSTALL.md](./INSTALL.md) for more installation options.

## Usage

```
  gdu [directory_to_scan] [flags]

Flags:
      --archive-browsing              Enable browsing of zip/jar archives
      --collapse-path                 Collapse single-child directory chains
      --config-file string            Read config from file (default is $HOME/.gdu.yaml)
  -D, --db string                     Store analysis in database (*.sqlite for SQLite, *.badger for BadgerDB)
      --depth int                     Show directory structure up to specified depth in non-interactive mode (0 means the flag is ignored)
      --enable-profiling              Enable collection of profiling data and provide it on http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/
  -E, --exclude-type strings          File types to exclude (e.g., --exclude-type yaml,json)
  -L, --follow-symlinks               Follow symlinks for files, i.e. show the size of the file to which symlink points to (symlinks to directories are not followed)
  -h, --help                          help for gdu
  -i, --ignore-dirs strings           Paths to ignore (separated by comma). Can be absolute or relative to current directory (default [/proc,/dev,/sys,/run])
  -I, --ignore-dirs-pattern strings   Path patterns to ignore (separated by comma)
  -X, --ignore-from string            Read path patterns to ignore from file
  -f, --input-file string             Import analysis from JSON file
  -l, --log-file string               Path to a logfile (default "/dev/null")
      --max-age string                Include files with mtime no older than DURATION (e.g., 7d, 2h30m, 1y2mo)
  -m, --max-cores int                 Set max cores that Gdu will use. 8 cores available (default 8)
      --min-age string                Include files with mtime at least DURATION old (e.g., 30d, 1w)
      --mouse                         Use mouse
  -c, --no-color                      Do not use colorized output
  -x, --no-cross                      Do not cross filesystem boundaries
      --no-delete                     Do not allow deletions
  -H, --no-hidden                     Ignore hidden directories (beginning with dot)
      --no-prefix                     Show sizes as raw numbers without any prefixes (SI or binary) in non-interactive mode
  -p, --no-progress                   Do not show progress in non-interactive mode
      --no-spawn-shell                Do not allow spawning shell
  -u, --no-unicode                    Do not use Unicode symbols (for size bar)
  -n, --non-interactive               Do not run in interactive mode
  -o, --output-file string            Export all info into file as JSON
  -r, --read-from-storage             Use existing database instead of re-scanning
      --reverse-sort                  Reverse sorting order (smallest to largest) in non-interactive mode
      --sequential                    Use sequential scanning (intended for rotating HDDs)
  -A, --show-annexed-size             Use apparent size of git-annex'ed files in case files are not present locally (real usage is zero)
  -a, --show-apparent-size            Show apparent size
  -d, --show-disks                    Show all mounted disks
  -k, --show-in-kib                   Show sizes in KiB (or kB with --si) in non-interactive mode
  -C, --show-item-count               Show number of items in directory
  -M, --show-mtime                    Show latest mtime of items in directory
  -B, --show-relative-size            Show relative size instead of percentage
  -S, --shared                        Count each device's size only once by ignoring bind mounts
  -s, --summarize                     Show only a total in non-interactive mode
      --si                            Show sizes with decimal SI prefixes (kB, MB, GB) instead of binary prefixes (KiB, MiB, GiB)
      --storage string                Storage backend to use in non-interactive mode (memory, sqlite, badger) (default "memory")
      --style string                  Predefined color style (default is your terminal's theme, also: dark, dark-bg)
  -g, --use-git-ignore                Use .gitignore
      --version                       Print version and exit
  -w, --write-config                  Write current configuration to file
```

### Examples

    gdu                                   # analyze current dir
    gdu -a                                # use apparent size instead of disk usage
    gdu <some_dir_to_analyze>             # analyze given dir
    gdu -d                                # show all mounted devices
    gdu -l ./gdu.log <some_dir>           # write errors to log file
    gdu -i /sys,/proc /                   # ignore some paths
    gdu -I '.*[abc]+$' /                  # ignore paths by regular pattern
    gdu -X ignore_file /                  # ignore paths in the file (one per line)
    gdu -c /                              # use only white/gray/black colors

    gdu -n /                              # non-interactive mode - write stats to stdout
    gdu -np /                             # do not show progress in non-interactive mode
    gdu / > file                          # write stats to file, do not show progress

    gdu -nps /                            # print total usage
    gdu -npc /                            # print items in the current directory

    gdu -f /path/to/file                  # read analysis data from JSON file
    gdu -o /path/to/file /                # write analysis data to JSON file

    gdu -d --db /path/to/db.sqlite /      # store analysis to SQLite database
    gdu -d --db /path/to/db.badger /      # store analysis to BadgerDB
    gdu -r --db /path/to/db.sqlite /      # read from existing database without re-scanning

## Keyboard shortcuts

```
  ↑ or k                      Move cursor up
  ↓ or j                      Move cursor down
  → or Enter or l             Go to highlighted directory
  ← or h                      Go to parent directory
  g                           Jump to the top of the listing
  G                           Jump to the bottom of the listing
  d                           Delete the selected file or directory
  e                           Empty the selected directory (delete its content)
  v                           Show content of the selected file
  o                           Open the selected file or directory with default application
  n                           Sort by name
  s                           Sort by size
  c                           Sort by item count
  m                           Sort by mtime
  a                           Toggle between showing disk usage and apparent size
  B                           Toggle between relative size/percentage
  C                           Show/hide item count
  M                           Show/hide latest mtime
  r                           Refresh/rescan the directory
  i                           Show/hide info about the selected directory
  I                           Show info about all mounted devices
  f                           Filter current directory by entering text or regular expression
  F                           Append filter rule (space separated)
  ^f or /                     Show only files matching the filter pattern (hide directories)
  !                           Negate the filter (show all but items matching the pattern)
  =                           Clear filter
  u                           Unmark all marked items
  space                       Mark/unmark highlighted item
  b                           Spawn shell in the current directory ($SHELL)
  q or Q or Ctrl+c            Quit gdu
```

## File flags

Files and directories may be prefixed by a one-character flag with following meaning:

* `!` An error occurred while reading this directory.

* `.` An error occurred while reading a subdirectory, i.e. total count is not exact.

* `@` File is symlink or socket.

* `H` Same file was already counted (hard link).

* `e` Directory is empty.

## Configuration file

Gdu can read (and write) YAML configuration file.

`$HOME/.config/gdu/gdu.yaml` and `$HOME/.gdu.yaml` are checked for the presence of the config file by default.

### Examples

* To configure gdu to permanently run in gray-scale color mode:

```
echo "no-color: true" >> ~/.gdu.yaml
```

* To set default sorting in configuration file:

```
sorting:
    by: name // size, name, itemCount, mtime
    order: desc
```

* To configure gdu to set CWD variable when browsing directories:

```
echo "change-cwd: true" >> ~/.gdu.yaml
```

* To save the current configuration

```
gdu --write-config
```

## Styling

There are wide options for how terminals can be colored.
Some gdu primitives (like basic text) adapt to different color schemas, but the selected/highlighted row does not.

If the default look is not sufficient, it can be changed in configuration file, e.g.:

```
style:
    selected-row:
        text-color: black
        background-color: "#ff0000"
```

## Deletion in background and in parallel (experimental)

Gdu can delete items in the background, thus not blocking the UI for additional work.
To enable:

```
echo "delete-in-background: true" >> ~/.gdu.yaml
```

Directory items can be also deleted in parallel, which might increase the speed of deletion.
To enable:

```
echo "delete-in-parallel: true" >> ~/.gdu.yaml
```

## Saving analysis data to database

Gdu can store the analysis data to a database file instead of just memory.
This allows you to save and reload analysis results later.
Both SQLite and BadgerDB are supported.

```
gdu --db analysis.sqlite /        # saves analysis data to SQLite database
gdu --db analysis.badger /        # saves analysis data to BadgerDB
gdu -r --db analysis.sqlite /     # reads saved data, does not run analysis again
```

{"command":"python3 - << 'PY'
import subprocess, os, shutil
def run(args, home="/tmp/fakehome_empty"):
    if os.path.exists(home): pass
    env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    print(args, "home=",home, r.returncode); print("OUT",r.stdout); print("ERR",r.stderr); print("---")
os.makedirs("/tmp/fakehome_empty",exist_ok=True)
# config sets no-hidden etc
open("/tmp/fakehome_empty/.gdu.yaml","w").write("no-hidden: true\nshow-apparent-size: true\n")
run(["-np","/tmp/testdir"])
# command line override? can't unset bool via flag... maybe --no-hidden=false?
run(["-np","--no-hidden=false","/tmp/testdir"])
run(["-np","--show-apparent-size=false","/tmp/testdir"])
# invalid yaml
open("/tmp/fakehome_empty/.gdu.yaml","w").write("::: not yaml: [")
run(["-np","/tmp/testdir"])
# unknown field
open("/tmp/fakehome_empty/.gdu.yaml","w").write("unknown-key: 123\n")
run(["-np","/tmp/testdir"])
# wrong type
open("/tmp/fakehome_empty/.gdu.yaml","w").write("no-hidden: notabool\n")
run(["-np","/tmp/testdir"])
# explicit config file missing
os.remove("/tmp/fakehome_empty/.gdu.yaml")
run(["-np","--config-file","/tmp/nonexist.yaml","/tmp/testdir"])
# explicit ??? default missing is ok
run(["-np","/tmp/testdir"])
# .config/gdu/gdu.yaml precedence
os.makedirs("/tmp/fakehome_empty/.config/gdu",exist_ok=True)
open("/tmp/fakehome_empty/.config/gdu/gdu.yaml","w").write("no-hidden: true\n")
open("/tmp/fakehome_empty/.gdu.yaml","w").write("show-apparent-size: true\n")
run(["-np","/tmp/testdir"])
PY"}

import subprocess, os, shutil
def clean(home):
    if os.path.exists(home): shutil.rmtree(home)
    os.makedirs(home)
def run(args, home):
    env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]=home
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    print(args,home,r.returncode,repr(r.stderr))
    for root,dirs,files in os.walk(home):
        for f in files:
            p=os.path.join(root,f)
            print(p,oct(os.stat(p).st_mode))
            print(open(p).read()[:500])
    print("---")
clean("/tmp/fh1")
run(["--write-config","-np","/tmp/testdir/sub1"],"/tmp/fh1")
# if .config/gdu/gdu.yaml exists, write there?
clean("/tmp/fh1"); os.makedirs("/tmp/fh1/.config/gdu"); open("/tmp/fh1/.config/gdu/gdu.yaml","w").write("no-color: true\n")
run(["--write-config","-np","/tmp/testdir/sub1"],"/tmp/fh1")
# explicit config file
clean("/tmp/fh1")
run(["--write-config","--config-file","/tmp/mycfg.yaml","-np","/tmp/testdir/sub1"],"/tmp/fh1")
print("mycfg exists",os.path.exists("/tmp/mycfg.yaml"))
if os.path.exists("/tmp/mycfg.yaml"): print(open("/tmp/mycfg.yaml").read()[:500], oct(os.stat("/tmp/mycfg.yaml").st_mode))
# flags reflect in written config
clean("/tmp/fh1")
run(["--write-config","-npcas","--si","--depth","2","--top","5","-i","/foo,/bar","-I","pat1","--mouse","/tmp/testdir/sub1"],"/tmp/fh1")
PY"}

import os, subprocess, time, shutil
base="/tmp/age_boundary"
if os.path.exists(base): shutil.rmtree(base)
os.makedirs(base)
now=int(time.time())
# create files aged N days exactly minus 12h to avoid execution edge: filenames age in days, mtime=now - N*86400 + 43200 (so age is N -0.5 day)
# Then max-age threshold in days: included if threshold >= age => threshold > N-0.5
cases=[28,29,30,31,32,60,90,364,365,366,730]
for n in cases:
    p=f"{base}/d{n}.txt"; open(p,"w").write("x"); t=now-n*86400+43200; os.utime(p,(t,t))
env=dict(os.environ); env["HOME"]="/tmp/fakehome_empty2"
def incl(flag,val):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","-np",flag,val,base],capture_output=True,text=True,env=env)
    return sorted([l.split()[-1] for l in r.stdout.splitlines()])
for val in ["1mo","2mo","3mo","1y","2y","30d","31d","365d"]:
    print(val, incl("--max-age",val))

S="gdu_style"; exe="/workspace/executable"

    if os.path.exists(home): shutil.rmtree(home)
    os.makedirs(home); open(home+"/.gdu.yaml","w").write(cfg)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-session","-t",S],capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s",S,"-x","80","-y","24",f"HOME={home} TERM=xterm-256color {exe} {args}"],check=True)
    time.sleep(.6)
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t",S,"-p","-e"],capture_output=True,text=True)

func runTUI(root *Node, flags *Flags, absPath, backend string, sqliteDB *sqliteStorage, ignoreDirs []string, pattern *regexp.Regexp, patterns []string, tf *timeFilter) error {
	ui := newTermUI(root, flags, absPath)
	ui.ignoreDirs = ignoreDirs
	ui.pattern = pattern
	ui.timeFilter = tf
	ui.backend = backend
	ui.sqliteDB = sqliteDB
	return ui.run()
}

func runTUIWithScan(flags *Flags, absPath, backend string, sqliteDB *sqliteStorage, scan *scanner, exporting bool, exportWriter *os.File) error {
	// The full TUI shows a scanning modal; for now scan synchronously
	// inside the interactive runner.
	root := scan.analyze(absPath)
	if backend == "sqlite" && sqliteDB != nil {
		if err := sqliteDB.storeTree(root, absPath); err == nil {
			if r, err := sqliteDB.loadTree(); err == nil && r != nil {
				root = r
			}
		}
	}
	if backend == "badger" {

	ui.pattern = scan.pattern
	ui.timeFilter = scan.timeF
	ui.backend = backend
	ui.sqliteDB = sqliteDB
	return ui.run()
}

		defer out.WriteString("\x1b[?1006l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1000l")
	}
	sb := newScreenBuf(out)

		sb.resize()

		if err != nil {

#!/bin/sh
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# The SQLite backend is implemented through cgo against the system
# libsqlite3. Install its headers on Debian-like systems when they are
# missing and installation is possible; on the evaluation image they
# are normally already present.
if [ ! -f /usr/include/sqlite3.h ]; then
    if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if [ "$(id -u)" = "0" ]; then
            apt-get update && apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev gcc
        elif command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
            sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev gcc
        fi
    fi
fi

export CGO_ENABLED=1
if [ -z "${GOCACHE:-}" ] && [ -z "${HOME:-}" ]; then
    GOCACHE="$(mktemp -d)"
    export GOCACHE
fi
export GOSUMDB=off
export GOTOOLCHAIN=local
if [ -d vendor ]; then
    export GOPROXY=off
    go build -mod=vendor -o executable .
else
    MODCACHE="$(go env GOMODCACHE 2>/dev/null || true)"
